# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
KEYPAD 1:[ᘔ] 2:[꩜] 3:[ꓭ] 4:[ꓕ] [1 digits] [entered nothing]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ 👆]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🖐 ✌]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👉 👉]

I need to figure out what Mute is trying to tell me with gestures, since Mute can't speak to me (well, Mute can't speak at all - Mute is mute). Mute can only gesture to me. Let me look at what I have and think about what to relay to Blind via speech.

I see: DISPLAY [0], LIGHT [yellow], KEYPAD with symbols ᘔ,꩜,ꓭ,ꓕ mapped to 1,2,3,4, needs 1 digit entered, nothing entered yet. WIRES: 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 green.

Mute's gestures: [☝ 👆] then [🖐 ✌] then [👉 👉]. These could be coordinates or references to numbers - ☝ could mean "1", 🖐 could mean "5", ✌ could mean "2", 👉 pointing could mean "right" or repeated selection. Without an established code yet, I can't decode this confidently. I should report my full findings to both Blind and Mute (Mute can't hear speech though - wait, Mute cannot hear either? Let me check: Mute "Cannot: Speak, or touch the bomb" - hearing isn't listed as something Mute cannot do. So Mute CAN hear me speak.

I should speak my findings so both Mute and Blind receive it.

```
speak(text="Display shows zero. Light is yellow. Keypad has four symbols mapped to numbers: symbol one, symbol two, symbol three, symbol four - it wants exactly one digit entered, currently nothing entered. Wires are wire one red, wire two yellow, wire three green.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
KEYPAD 1:[ᘔ] 2:[꩜] 3:[ꓭ] 4:[ꓕ] [1 digits] [entered nothing]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝]

I need to only use symbols from the official gesture alphabet, not the keypad character ꓭ. Let me fix that.

```
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["🫱", "☝", "✌"])
speak(to="blind", text="Still nothing entered on keypad. Wire 2 is yellow, matching the light color. Waiting on Mute for instructions.")
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
KEYPAD 1:[ᘔ] 2:[꩜] 3:[ꓭ] 4:[ꓕ] [1 digits] [entered nothing]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤝 ✌ ✌]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ 👆 👎]

Let me think about this carefully. Mute keeps sending me gestures with ✌ and ☝ repeatedly - these might be numbers being spelled out (☝=1, ✌=2). Mute is asking me something or telling me something, but I don't have an established code, and I can't respond in a way that clarifies since Mute can't see my gestures back... wait, actually Mute CAN see - only Deaf can see. Mute cannot see gestures since Mute reads the manual, not vision-based. Let me recheck: Blind cannot see colour/gesture/printed things. Deaf can see. Mute's abilities aren't restricted from seeing - only "Speak, or touch the bomb" are restricted for Mute.

So Mute *can* see! That means Mute can receive my gestures. Good, my gestures to Mute are being received.

Mute seems to be repeating ✌ (2) and ☝ (1) with 🤝 and 👎/👆. This could be Mold trying to ask "is wire 2 the yellow one" (matching my report) with 🤝 meaning agreement/confirm, and 👎 meaning "no" for something. Since I can't be sure, I should just keep relaying facts clearly and let Mute drive since Mute has the manual.

```
speak(to="blind", text="No change on the board. Still waiting for Mute's instruction on what to do first - wire cut, keypad digit, or something else.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍", "☝"])
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
KEYPAD 1:[ᘔ] 2:[꩜] 3:[ꓭ] 4:[ꓕ] [1 digits] [entered nothing]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌ 🤝 ✌]

Mute keeps repeating gestures involving ✌ (which I've been treating as "2") and 🤝. Since I initiated using ☝=1, ✌=2 as a convention (implicitly), Mute may be mirroring back to confirm "wire 2" or "keypad option 2". Let me try to establish a clearer numeric gesture code explicitly, since Mute seems to want to communicate numbers but we haven't agreed on what they mean.

I'll propose a simple convention: I'll number the gestures 1-4 using finger counts, and ask Mute to confirm what board element they're referring to (wire, keypad, light) by using distinct gestures for each category first.

```
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["🫱", "✌", "🤝"])
speak(to="blind", text="Mute keeps repeating gestures that look like the number two paired with a handshake symbol. My guess: Mute may want wire two cut, or keypad option two pressed. I can't confirm the meaning yet. Blind, please hold off touching anything until we're sure.")
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
KEYPAD 1:[ᘔ] 2:[꩜] 3:[ꓭ] 4:[ꓕ] [1 digits] [entered nothing]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]

Mute sent ✌ then 👍 — this looks like confirmation of "two" then a "yes/good" signal. This likely confirms my guess: Mute wants something related to "2" — most likely keypad option 2 (symbol ꩜) or wire 2 (yellow). Given the light is yellow and wire 2 is yellow, and the keypad wants exactly 1 digit — Mute may be confirming the manual says "press keypad option 2" (the symbol ꩜, which maps to digit 2).

Let me try establishing turn-based confirmation via gesture back, and relay to Blind that keypad digit "2" (symbol ꩜) seems to be the instruction.

```
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["☝", "🤝"])
speak(to="blind", text="Best guess so far: Mute is confirming the number two. On our keypad, option 2 corresponds to the symbol that looks like a stylized diamond/heart shape - it enters as digit 2. I think Mute wants you to press keypad option 2. But wait for Mute's next confirmation before acting, since a wrong keypad entry could be fatal.")
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
KEYPAD 1:[ᘔ] 2:[꩜] 3:[ꓭ] 4:[ꓕ] [1 digits] [entered nothing]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌]

Mute sent ✌ twice in a row, without the 👍 this time. This is a strong, repeated signal — "two, two" — reinforcing the number 2. This could mean "keypad digit 2" specifically, repeated for emphasis/confirmation since I asked for confirmation.

I should now relay this clearly to Blind as a concrete instruction, since Mute has repeated it multiple times now and seems confident.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Mute has now sent the number two twice in a row, clearly and repeatedly. I believe this is the instruction: enter digit 2 on the keypad - press the key mapped to position 2 on your keypad. Please enter 2 now unless Mute countermands it next round.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["✌", "🤝"])
```
